close_reason: Won't fix: opinion-tagged. Reviewer concludes 'modern Rust APIs lean toward bool + builder-with-defaults, not three-variant Tristate enums.' Option<bool> matches the wire (None=key absent, Some(true)=true, Some(false)=false) and is widely understood. Reopen if a concrete user reports confusion.
description:
Public method signatures use `Option<bool>` for nearly every flag:
- calendar_set: on_destroy_remove_events: Option<bool> (calendar.rs:79)
- calendar_event_query: expand_recurrences: Option<bool> (event.rs:132)
- principal_get_availability: show_details: Option<bool> (principal_availability.rs:19)
- CalendarEventGetParams.{expand_recurrences, reduced_participants, fetch_calendars}: Option<bool> (mod.rs:165-173)

The /review-rusty rules call this out specifically: 'Option<bool> in a public API. This is almost always a three-variant enum (Yes, No, Unknown / Inherited / NotSet) with meaningful names.'

Three states the wire really has:
- key absent → server uses spec default (typically false)
- "someFlag": true
- "someFlag": false

These are NOT semantically equivalent to None/Some(true)/Some(false). Wire-absent means 'server uses default'; the spec defaults differ per flag (e.g. expandRecurrences defaults to false; showDetails defaults to false). For a caller saying 'I want the spec default,' Option<bool>::None is more cryptic than a named variant.

Lower priority because the cost is paper-cutty: callers writing `expand_recurrences: Some(true)` is verbose, and the asymmetry between `Some(true)` and `None` (which both reach the server as 'true' for some flags depending on default) is confusing only if you read the spec carefully.

Probably an opinion-tier flag — modern Rust APIs lean toward bool + builder-with-defaults, not three-variant Tristate enums. But the type-design rule is clear, so noting it.
title: expand_recurrences/show_details/etc accept Option<bool> with no third state
